newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia gas oil swaps dives on intense sell pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia gas oil swaps dives on intense sell pressure.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil swaps collapsed early afternoon on Wednesday after a massive selloff triggered by oil majors coming out to sell the paper on weak regional fundamentals and as crude values lost steam, traders said.
"Gas oil just collapsed after some majors came out to sell which spooked an already weak market," a trader said.
Almost every other trading companies came out to sell, sparked off by the majors' selloff, while buyers were restricted to Chinese traders and some banks.

July swaps were last offered at $20.00 per barrel with no firm sellers seen against it compared to Tuesday's $20.90/$21.00, brokers said. July traded in the morning at $20.68 and $20.70 but in the afternoon deals were seen at $20.30 and $20.00, they said.
Some traders said they would be surprised if July plunged below $20.00.
August lost more ground compared to July as the market which was earlier expecting demand to pick up in August lost confidence and also began selling the next front month, traders said.

August was last quoted at $20.40/$20.60 down about $1.20 from Tuesday while at the same time narrowing the July/August spread to value at around minus 50 cents from a morning value of about minus 90 cents, brokers said.
August traded in the morning at $21.70 and $21.65 and collapsed in the afternoon to trade at $21.50, $21.45, $21.25, $21.00, $20.90, $20.80, brokers said.
Brokers said the most recent trade done was for September at $21.65 with the August/September spread valued at minus $1.10 per barrel.
Traders said the fresh sell pressure was due to the sustained aggressive physical offers late Tuesday which still failed to draw out buyers.
On Tuesday, July gas oil was offered to a low of $20.80 per barrel, down 50 cents from Tuesday's lowest offered level.
"Gas oil was offered below $21.00 for the first time in over a year but still no one was interested in buying. The market is quite despressed," a trader said.
Gas oil prices are at their lowest level since October 1995 and traders said the near term outlook is not promising due to the lack of fresh regional demand.
Traders said with buyers still expected to stay away, physical values could drop below the lowest prompt level of $20.05 seen in October 1995.
India's unexpectedly low 165,000 tonnet award for August delivery cargoes on Monday compared to the 855,000 tonne awarded for July initiated the sell off, traders said.
Abundant supplies in the MidEast could see cargoes coming this way in August, adding on to high stocks in Singapore and South Korea.

Major buyer China's continued absence in the third quarter was expected to worsen gas oil values and even Indonesia's additional requirements for August were not expected to help curb a freefall, traders said.
